utterances.text: In the moment you started your negotiations, you have been aware that the 12 Serbs has been in the control of Murat Sabanovic, in fact, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-022
utterances.text: No. No, that statement is not true. When we talked I talked with Savovic who had the authority to negotiate on behalf of the SDS or the Crisis Staff, whatever it was that they called themselves. Those people were near a construction company called Granit in the building of a restaurant there, and that's where I saw them too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Murat Sabanovic and his men have been armed in this time? They have control over the dam?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-022
utterances.text: Yes, they were armed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreter did not hear the rest of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Of whose sentence, the sentence of -- you mean you didn't hear the rest of the answer?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The rest of the answer, Your Honour, was: "And they were at the dam."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: But Murat Sabanovic and his men were not members of ordinary police. True?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-022
utterances.text: No, they were not members of the ordinary police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: And the moment they capture the dam they were not members of any ordinary armed forces.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-022
utterances.text: Well, if you will allow me to clarify. When the need arose, the authorities of the municipality of Visegrad would mobilise the so-called reserve police force and the Territorial Defence. They were officially on lists as reserve police force members or reserve Territorial Defence members, and such units, at the call of municipal authorities, could also be joined by all who thought that they should join. So such units would thereby be enlarged in number, both the police units and the Territorial Defence units. And one could say that they were part of the Territorial Defence units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: During your testimony in the Vasiljevic case, you told under oath that Murat Sabanovic came there on his own initiative with his own group of men. Is it your statement, your testimony in the Vasiljevic case or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-022
utterances.text: I do not recall this statement exactly, but I can say that that is the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. In your first negotiations you talked about conditions for release of the 12 Serbs. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-022
utterances.text: Yes, it would be fair to say that it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: In the first negotiations you have participated, it was said that the 12 Serbs will be released if there will be a cease-fire. Is it true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-022
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: And in your testimony in the Vasiljevic procedure - this is page 143 on the English transcript - you used the term "we." Is it true that you described your activities as negotiator and you described your position using the term "we"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-022
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do not understand. I do not sufficiently understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Reformulate. Reformulate the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that in the negotiations you -- your function was an envoy or a messenger of the intentions of the group of Murat Sabanovic? Is it true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-022
utterances.text: No. Your Honours, if I can amplify on that. All the activities that were referred to, that we have been talking about actually have nothing whatsoever to do with Murat Sabanovic and his group. They impacted in no way whatsoever the course of the negotiations or could they actually dictate any conditions as to what was to be the object or the substance of the negotiations or anything of the -- that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: I would like to -- to quote from page 143, line 8 up to 11 of the English transcript of your testimony in the Vasiljevic case. "We discussed the release of the people that had been taken into custody, and our side, if I can use the term, called for a cease-fire, for an end to the mortars shelling Muslim villages and parts of the town, and we said that the two days later we -- they would be released." So you used the term "we" as if you are part of this group. You do not -- you did not transfer a message, you were part of this. Do you agree with me that this is your statement in the Vasiljevic case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-022
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, that is identical. That is completely true. But when I used this word "we," what was certainly meant was the structure of the authorities, because I conducted these negotiations in coordination with the president of the Assembly, the president of the -- of the Executive Board, the chief of the police who all comprised what is referred to as the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Visegrad. So when I say "we," I mean that group, and I was sort of an envoy of that Crisis Staff to conduct the negotiations that we have been discussing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: VG-22, are you aware of an order for Mr. Savovic to the Serb police before these dates that all Serbs have to left the old police station? Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-022
utterances.text: Well, I'm not directly aware of that, but I suppose that that was the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about the decision to exclude Sredoje Lukic being a member of the ordinary police before the beginning of April 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-022
utterances.text: No. I have not any knowledge about any decisions having been taken or supposed to have been taken to chuck out Sredoje Lukic from the regular police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: When I understood you correctly, your only argument to say that Sredoje Lukic was not a member of the Serbian police any more was that he was not taking part in ordinary service any more. Did I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-022
utterances.text: Well, you could put it that way. If a policeman fails to show up for work, does not report to his superiors and what have you and what have you not, one can assume that he has left the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that this behaviour of Sredoje Lukic, taking it as truth, could also be following the order of Mr. Savovic? Couldn't it be, just to leave the old police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-022
utterances.text: Yes. In my opinion that was the reason why he and other policemen as well ceased coming to work, to their regular work posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: So to sum it up, VG-22, would you agree with me to say that in the moment you started your negotiations, 12 Serbs including Serbian policemen has been arrested and kept by irregular armed Muslim forces and that you have used this fact of this arrest as a bargaining chip in your negotiations? Couldn't you say it in this way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-022
utterances.text: I will agree with you, with the statement for the most part, provided, however, that these men, these arrested men, these armed men were not under the control of some informal groups or something -- some similar structure. They were always at all times under the control of the regular police or the Territorial Defence. So let me add if the need arose for them to be moved from the police station to another facility or -- because the situation was almost a state of war, that facility was controlled by the Territorial Defence. They would be handed over to them, but always with the knowledge and approval of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: A last question from my side, VG-22. Is it true to say that if a Serb did act against orders of the White Eagles that the consequences would be the same as someone who did so as a Muslim? Do you agree with this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-022
utterances.text: Yes, one could say that. I wouldn't say identical, the same. I would say almost the same, practically the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dieckmann. Mr. Ossogo, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, that concludes your testimony. We thank you for giving it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution calls Mr. Ferid Spahic to the witness stand, and he does not wish to have any protective measures. He renounced his protective measures in the Vasiljevic case, and he's not requesting them in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Lukic has indicated to me that he's not feeling well right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. We will adjourn for 10 minutes. --- Break taken at 11.38 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Mr. Milan Lukic is too ill to come back, and I would ask for a recess until tomorrow considering the short duration we have left for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
